title: Al grito de: la consigna que impulsa una movilización

sections.content: Al grito de (to the cry of, rallying behind the slogan) introduces the specific chant or slogan that drove a protest, uprising, or mobilization -- vivid and concrete, common in historical narration of social movements. It's followed by a quoted slogan. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: La CONAIE organizó el primer gran levantamiento indígena nacional, al grito de "¡Nada solo para los indios, todo para todos!".
items.english: CONAIE organized the country's first great national Indigenous uprising, to the cry of "Nothing just for Indians, everything for everyone!"

items.spanish: El EZLN se levantó en armas, al grito de "¡Ya basta!", exigiendo tierra, trabajo, vivienda y democracia.
items.english: The EZLN rose up in arms, to the cry of "Enough already!", demanding land, work, housing, and democracy.

items.spanish: Miles de manifestantes marcharon al grito de consignas que exigían el reconocimiento inmediato de sus derechos territoriales.
items.english: Thousands of protesters marched to the cry of slogans demanding immediate recognition of their territorial rights.

items.spanish: El movimiento se extendió rápidamente al grito de un lema que resumía, en pocas palabras, sus demandas centrales.
items.english: The movement spread rapidly rallying behind a slogan that summed up, in a few words, its central demands.

sections.content: Al grito de works best right before a quoted slogan in quotation marks -- it's a compact way to fold the movement's own words directly into the narration, rather than describing the slogan indirectly.
